title: Power Apps: responsive, multi-column starting layout for SharePoint list forms (preview)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, responsive-layout behaviour and environment-setting command are supported. Minor corrections should clarify existing licensing and billing rules, acknowledge the alternative maker role, and reconcile governance guidance with the controls table.

claims.claim: Power Apps introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new SharePoint customized forms.
claims.quote: The public preview of SharePoint Customize Forms introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new forms in eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a public preview for eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.
claims.quote: The public preview of SharePoint Customize Forms introduces a responsive, multi-column starting layout for new forms in eligible commercial SharePoint tenants.

claims.claim: Makers can customize these forms while preserving their connection to SharePoint list actions.
claims.quote: Makers can customize these forms while preserving their connection to SharePoint list actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival, so the default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive new forms template enable disable tenant eligibility rollout preview November 2026. Opened sharepoint-form-integration; read roadmap record. Learn says 'where it's enabled' but neither source specifies activation or rollout defaults.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.
claims.quote: The previous template used a mobile-sized canvas with a single-column form.

claims.claim: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type.
claims.quote: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and a responsive layout that adapts to the available space.

claims.claim: The responsive layout adapts to the available space.
claims.quote: The new template uses the Flexible canvas type and a responsive layout that adapts to the available space.

claims.claim: Learn describes the responsive template where it is enabled for new form creation.
claims.quote: This article describes the responsive template where it's enabled for new form creation.

claims.claim: Existing customized forms are not automatically converted to the responsive template.
claims.quote: Existing customized forms keep their current layout and aren't automatically converted.

claims.claim: Makers reach customization from their list through Integrate > Power Apps > Customize forms.
claims.quote:
Open your list in SharePoint or Microsoft Lists.
Select Integrate > Power Apps > Customize forms.

claims.claim: The generated form uses one column below app width 640.
claims.quote: If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))

claims.claim: The generated form uses two columns from app width 640 to below 900.
claims.quote: If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))

claims.claim: The generated form uses three columns at app width 900 or more.
claims.quote: If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Column breakpoints use app width and do not guarantee the number that fits every SharePoint panel, so Learn advises testing in the actual host.
claims.quote:
The form's NumberOfColumns formula uses the app's width:
If(App.Width < 640, 1, If(App.Width < 900, 2, 3))
These app-width breakpoints don't guarantee how many columns fit inside every SharePoint panel. Check the form in its actual host, not only in Studio.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: SharePointIntegration actions OnNew, OnView, OnEdit, OnSave and OnCancel handle the list's corresponding operations and should be preserved.
claims.quote: Preserve the generated actions so the nested form responds to the list's New, View, Edit, Save, and Cancel operations:

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises keeping the generated layout containers and responsive formulas during customization.
claims.quote: Keep the form inside its layout containers. Change the title, description, and fields without replacing responsive sizing formulas with fixed values.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Replacing generated data-card formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns with fixed values can stop fields from reflowing.
claims.quote: Generated data cards use formulas based on Parent.NumberOfColumns for their position and width. Replacing those formulas with fixed values can stop fields from reflowing.

claims.claim: The form's DataSource stays bound to the customized SharePoint list.
claims.quote: The form's DataSource is the list you customize.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Users with at least Read or Restricted View on the linked SharePoint list inherit access to the customized form.
claims.quote: Instead, any user who has at least Read or Restricted View access to the linked SharePoint list inherits access to the form.

claims.claim: Users given permissions only to specific list items do not have access to the customized form.
claims.quote: Users who have only been given permissions to specific items in the list don't have access to the customized form.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn do not describe an identity change for the new template.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive customized form template data sources identity autonomous actions SharePointIntegration. Opened sharepoint-form-integration and read roadmap record; neither describes an identity change.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for this layout change.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive customized form template data sources identity autonomous actions SharePointIntegration. Opened sharepoint-form-integration and read roadmap record; documented generated actions respond to list operations, with no new autonomous behaviour described.

claims.claim: Learn advises against imperative functions such as Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties.
claims.quote: Don't use imperative functions such as Launch() in SharePointIntegration properties such as OnNew and OnView.

claims.claim: SharePointIntegration events can run in the background when the form is not visible.
claims.quote: These events can run in the background even when the form isn't visible.

claims.claim: Learn says Power Apps currently has no automated method to copy a form between environments.
claims.quote: While you can manually copy a form from one environment to another, there's currently no automated method in Power Apps to copy a form from one environment to another.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to the new template has been published.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites
A subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Use notes: 'The general SharePoint integration page requires a subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform. No requirement specific to the responsive template is published.' Replace the broad preview/GA licensing-unknown sentence and cost-rationale clause with 'No licensing requirement specific to the responsive template is published.' The prerequisite source is https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/customize-list-form; the existing licensing overview explains limited Microsoft 365 rights and premium requirements.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The SharePoint forms integration article names no prerequisite licence or licence specific to the responsive layout.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint responsive form template licensing requirements customized form standard connectors license Power Apps; SharePoint custom forms license Power Apps. Opened sharepoint-form-integration, customize-list-form and pricing-billing-skus; no layout-specific licence in the feature article.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The general SharePoint integration page lists a subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform as a prerequisite.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites
A subscription to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Power Platform.

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 licences include limited Power Apps use rights for Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.
claims.quote: Some Microsoft 365 licenses include limited Power Apps and Power Automate use rights. These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors.

claims.claim: Standalone licences provide premium capabilities beyond the limited Microsoft 365 use rights.
claims.quote: These use rights are intended for scenarios that use Microsoft 365 data and standard connectors. They don't provide the same rights as standalone premium licenses.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for this feature at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint customized responsive forms licensing standard connectors premium pay as you go meter. Opened sharepoint-form-integration, pricing-billing-skus and pay-as-you-go-meters; no separate responsive-layout meter, but existing app metering is documented.
claims.fix: Replace the meter sentence with 'No separate meter is documented for the responsive layout at the time of writing (November 2026); existing Power Apps billing rules still apply.' In the cost rationale, replace 'names no licence or meter' with 'names no layout-specific licence or meter'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn advises checking the customized form at each layout size.
claims.quote: Check long labels, multiline fields, required-field messages, and scrolling at each layout size.

claims.claim: Creating a custom SharePoint form creates a canvas app in the default environment unless another form environment is designated.
claims.quote: When a maker creates a custom SharePoint form in SharePoint, it creates a canvas app in the default environment. To avoid cluttering the default environment with these apps, create a separate environment to store custom SharePoint forms.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName '<EnvironmentName>' designates where newly created SharePoint custom forms are saved.
claims.quote:
Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment -EnvironmentName 'EnvironmentName'
This command designates the environment newly created SharePoint custom forms save to, instead of the default environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a Power Platform admin center path for designating the SharePoint form environment.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps SharePoint custom forms designate environment admin center UI Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment. Opened powerapps-powershell, manage-default-environment and admin-manage-apps; designation uses PowerShell, not a documented admin center setting.

claims.claim: Only tenant admins can call the form-environment designation command.
claims.quote: Modifies which environment Power Platform users save Sharepoint form apps. Only tenant admins can call this command.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Only a production environment can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.
claims.quote: Only production environment can be designated for SharePoint custom forms.

claims.claim: Changing the designated environment does not automatically migrate existing custom forms.
claims.quote: Existing custom forms don't automatically migrate to the newly designated environment.

claims.claim: Deleting the designated SharePoint form environment deletes its custom forms.
claims.quote: If the designated SharePoint custom form environment is deleted, the custom forms are deleted with it.

claims.claim: The PowerShell overview says creating a custom form in a designated environment requires Environment Maker.
claims.quote: The ability for a user to create a custom form in a designated environment requires that user to have the Environment Maker role.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of the final paragraph with 'The PowerShell overview says creators need Environment Maker, while Manage Power Apps documents the SharePoint custom form maker role as an alternative in a nondefault environment with Dataverse.' Both pages are already cited; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/admin-manage-apps explicitly accepts either role.

claims.claim: Distinguishing SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment.
claims.quote: The ability to distinguish SharePoint custom form makers from general Environment Makers requires Dataverse in the environment where the privilege is to be changed.

claims.claim: The SharePoint custom form maker role can limit makers to creating and editing SharePoint custom forms in a nondefault environment.
claims.quote: Outside of the default environment, an admin can unassign the Environment Maker security role from users and assign the SharePoint custom form maker security role.

claims.claim: The environment control is documented for SharePoint custom forms generally, rather than naming the responsive template specifically.
claims.quote: The Set-AdminPowerAppSharepointFormEnvironment cmdlet applies only to SharePoint forms customized by Power Apps.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of controls[0].note, in both representations, with 'Applies to SharePoint forms customized by Power Apps.' Replace the prose sentence beginning 'Neither page says' with 'These environment controls cover SharePoint forms customized by Power Apps.' This is the documented reach at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/guidance/adoption/manage-default-environment#designate-a-sharepoint-form-environment.

claims.fix: Remove the final sentence of Governance controls about the undocumented layout switch. Keep the existing question about retaining the previous template in Open questions; do not add a control row.
